prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: Across the five frames, the depth map captures an outdoor park layout with a foreground lawn and paved path, a curved stone retaining wall (~1.5–3 m left in Frame 2), a pavilion (~6–15 m away), and background trees as the camera wearer pans left then right and back. In Frame 1, a capped person stands ~1–1.5 m directly in front facing and looking toward the wearer with a raised purple frisbee in their right hand and a small object in their left, while a woman in sunglasses stands ~1.5–2 m to the lower left (~0.5–1 m from the capped person, partly cropped at the bottom-left edge) also facing the camera. As the wearer turns left in Frame 2, their own gloved left hand holding a blue frisbee appears within ~0.3–0.5 m at the lower left while a companion's head is partly visible ~1 m at the bottom-right edge; panning right across Frame 3 reveals a standing figure ~5–7 m away on the right and a tree trunk ~8–10 m ahead that are severely obscured by backlighting and shadow in the RGB image. In Frames 4 and 5, as the camera faces the pavilion and then widens out, the depth gradient orders the capped person in the near foreground (~1–1.5 m in Frame 4 with a raised right hand near arm's reach; ~1.5–2 m at the right edge of Frame 5, partially occluding the woman ~1 m behind them), the woman (~2.5–3.5 m away), and a third man holding a bottle ~2.5–3 m on the far left of Frame 5, all facing toward the wearer. The map is unreliable where very close surfaces saturate to uniform white—losing fine depth relief on the hand and frisbee in Frame 2 and the capped person's torso in Frame 4—and where the shadowed person's head in Frame 3 merges into the background foliage.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates foreground people and held frisbees across the camera wearer's head turns, separating the partially cropped woman on the lower left and the central capped person (~0.5–1 m apart and ~1–2 m from the wearer, both facing the camera) along with the raised frisbee within the capped person's right-hand reach in Frame 1. In Frame 2, it segments the camera wearer's own extended left arm and held frisbee (~0.3–0.5 m in front) on the left and a partially visible person ~1 m away at the bottom-right edge, while also detecting three distant cars (~20–30 m away) along the background road that are hard to pick out in the RGB strip. After showing no masks in Frame 3, it tracks the group's relative positions in Frames 4 and 5: the woman (~2.5–3.5 m away) and the nearer capped person (~1–2 m away to her right, cut off below the chest in Frame 4 and at the right frame edge in Frame 5 where they partially occlude her left side) stand ~1–1.5 m apart facing the wearer, while a third person enters ~2.5–3 m on the far left of Frame 5 (~4–5 m from the pair on the right). However, the map provides no distance gradients or orientation cues within masks and omits static park structures in Frames 1–4, making it unreliable for overall scene layout. It also exhibits severe classification and boundary errors, splitting the capped person's raised right arm into separate person masks and a false car label in Frame 1, mislabeling part of the stone wall as a person in Frame 2, completely missing the shadowed person in Frame 3 and held discs in Frame 5, and misclassifying the background pavilion and stone wall (~5–10 m behind the people) as a massive boat in Frame 5.
descriptions.pose: The pose map renders sparse 2D yellow body skeletons for only three human instances across the five-frame pan and omits all background layout, objects, and magenta hand skeletons. In Frame 1, it captures the upper body and facial keypoints of the capped person ~1–1.5 m directly in front of the camera wearer, showing symmetrical shoulders facing forward, eyes and nose oriented toward the camera, and both arms raised above shoulder height where the frisbee and small object are held. As the camera turns left in Frame 2 and pans right in Frame 3, the map misses the wearer's close-up left arm (~0.3–0.5 m) and the partial person on the right in Frame 2, but detects a tilted body and leg skeleton in the right-center of Frame 3 (~5–7 m away), revealing the posture of a person standing in deep shadow that is difficult to discern in the RGB frame alone. In Frame 4, it captures the upper torso, forward-facing head keypoints, and raised right arm (near the neck) of the woman standing ~2.5–3 m away on the left-center, showing her facing toward the camera wearer. The map is highly unreliable for complete multi-person tracking because it misses every other visible person—the cropped woman on the left in Frame 1, the close capped person (~1–1.5 m on the right) in Frame 4, and all three companions standing ~1.5–3.5 m away in Frame 5—as well as all lower bodies cut off by the frame edges and all fine finger articulations.
